name: Necrobiosis Lipoidica

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Necrobiosis Lipoidica

criteria.description: Presence of well-demarcated yellowish-brown atrophic plaques with telangiectasias, typically on the shins
Histological evidence of necrobiosis with granulomatous inflammation and thickened blood vessel walls
Presence of diabetes mellitus or impaired glucose tolerance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical plaques plus confirmatory histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by biopsy; diabetes association is common but not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Yellowish atrophic plaques with telangiectasias on shins
searchTerms: yellow thin skin patches with small blood vessels
yellowish skin spots with visible veins
shiny yellow skin lesions on shins

common.symptomName: Ulceration of plaques following minor trauma
Shiny, atrophic skin texture within plaques

occasional.symptomName: Peripheral neuropathy symptoms in affected limbs
occasional.notes: May be related to underlying diabetes
searchTerms: nerve damage symptoms in arms or legs
loss of sensation in affected limbs

occasional.symptomName: Delayed wound healing in ulcerated areas

rare.symptomName: Secondary bacterial infection of ulcerated plaques
Development of squamous cell carcinoma within chronic lesions
searchTerms: skin cancer developing in chronic lesions
squamous cell carcinoma in long-term skin patches

rare.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as low-grade fever

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated blood glucose or HbA1c in diabetic patients
Non-specific inflammatory markers may be mildly elevated
imaging: Doppler ultrasound may show normal or mildly reduced blood flow in affected skin
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations identified
other: Skin biopsy showing necrobiosis of collagen with palisading granulomatous inflammation and thickened blood vessel walls

distinguishingFeatures: Lesions are usually smaller, skin-colored to erythematous papules or plaques without atrophy or telangiectasias
Histology shows necrobiotic granulomas but lacks thickened blood vessels
Lesions are smaller, brownish, round or oval macules without atrophy or telangiectasias
Usually asymptomatic and located on shins
Associated with venous stasis signs such as edema, varicosities
Lesions are more erythematous, scaly, and less well-demarcated

redFlags: Rapid ulceration or non-healing ulcers within plaques
Signs of secondary infection such as increased pain, purulent discharge, or fever
Development of nodules or masses within chronic lesions suggesting malignant transformation
references: Bolognia JL, Schaffer JV, Cerroni L. Dermatology. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2018.
James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
Wang J, et al. Necrobiosis lipoidica: a review of clinical features and treatment. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2020;83(3):e145-e154.
